source.title: Conditional Co-Ablation: Recovering Self-Repair Backups in Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Z. Gong; Heng-Yang Lu; Tian-Tong Wang; Yi-Chi Zhang; Yi-Xin Wang; Zi-Hao Zeng; Ming-Gan Xiao; Chau Yuen; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

page_placements.theme: Backup and suppression heads: how they are located and what triggers them

record.tranche_reason: Tests conditional self-repair and backup recruitment with a two-state co-ablation score, rather than reproducing the original layer-ablation measurement. It reports causal repair and circuit-completion results.
record.gate_note: The study tests conditional backup recruitment and circuit completion. It also compares backup-recovery rankings against intact-state and conditional controls. The eight-model completion results use held-out induction behavior, not general-text full-distribution measurements. Cited results about other self-repair mechanisms are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: Mainly a method paper (CoAx), but it reports its own GPT-2-small IOI self-repair measurements. After zero-ablating the three primary name-movers, the IO−S margin falls only from 2.57 to 2.29. The documented backup branch's direct-logit contribution rises from +0.57 to +1.68. Freezing the backups removes part of the repair. Primaries-plus-backups ablation is non-additive (1.30 joint versus 0.67 summed). Intact single-ablation saliency ranks the backups near chance. These bear on V4, V5 and V7 by a different method than the originals. The cross-model and cross-mechanism results measure CoAx selection quality, not how much compensation occurs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors conclude that removing a primary circuit recruits dormant backups that become causally load-bearing, so intact-state circuits are incomplete under intervention. They also conclude that CoAx recovers those backups and completes the circuit. The cross-model and cross-mechanism evidence is about CoAx completions beating random and agreeing with freezing-based repair, not direct measurements of self-repair in those models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses conditional co-ablation: contrasts candidate-head ablation effects with the primary set present versus jointly removed, ranking growth in effect magnitude. This differs from the original layer-level Hydra intervention and the broader mechanism analyses in the cited self-repair work.
record.method_sensitivity: Backup recovery varies with the identity and contamination of the supplied primary set, the ablation replacement operator, the output geometry, and task/prompt setting. Correct IOI primary-set removal gives about 0.94 AUC, whereas matched wrong sets give about 0.40 AUC. Mean, resample, and Gaussian replacement give CoAx AUCs from 0.961 to 0.974. The cross-model results use repeated-token induction and a held-out completion metric.

fits_no_version.finding: Across eight non-GPT-2 models, adding CoAx-selected heads to a detected primary induction set increases held-out induction damage by 1.88–22.46× over size-matched random heads. CoAx growth also correlates with freezing-based repair in 11/12 instances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional co-ablation growth identifies heads that become load-bearing after primary-set removal across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: CoAx ranks the documented backups at 0.941 AUC, versus 0.665 for AtP* and 0.758 for conditional energy, and falls to about 0.40 for matched wrong primary sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An intact-to-removed two-state contrast is needed to locate dormant backups; recovery is specific to the removed circuit.

record.problems: Ground-truth documented backup labels are available only for GPT-2-small IOI. Broader evaluation uses different, task-specific causal-repair and induction-completion measures. The study conditions on a supplied primary set; automatic primary-set discovery is not tested. The MLP-group implementation check is mentioned without an outcome.

untested.parts: All of it. There are no layer-level ablations and no measurement of compensation by later attention layers.
All of it. The MLP-group implementation check (Appendix C.5.3) reports no result.
All of it. Self-repair is measured only on GPT-2-small IOI, a narrow task. The cross-model panel reports CoAx completion gains, not compensation on general text.
Prompt-level variation in compensation and overcorrection beyond the original effect are not reported.
Copy-suppression heads, anti-erasure neurons, and the share of self-repair carried by final-LayerNorm rescaling are not quantified.
Compensation magnitude (margin preservation, backup direct-logit gain) under mean or resample ablation is not reported. Only CoAx ranking AUC is given, and only on GPT-2-small IOI.
Other models and tasks, and the general size of attribution error, are not tested.

missing.what: Joint versus summed ablation. Primaries: summed singles 0.30, joint 0.28. Backups: 0.37 summed, 0.30 joint. Primaries plus backups: 0.67 summed, 1.30 joint (1.9×). A random set is approximately additive.
LayerNorm freezing raises backup AUC from 0.941 to 0.983. Backups retain 81% of their conditional growth (0.076→0.062), while non-backup growth turns negative (−0.001→−0.030).

Graded wake-up. Backup output-norm ratio goes 1.000→1.150 and conditional effect 0.046→0.102 as 0–3 primaries are removed; random heads stay flat. Dose response: as primary scaling α goes 0→1, margin falls 2.583→2.357 and backup wake rises 1.000→1.150.
Non-backup heads' summed IO−S contribution shifts from −0.773 to +0.392 after primary removal, so compensation extends beyond the documented backups.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows are method-performance results (CoAx versus baselines) and are relinked to none. Self-repair evidence is confined to GPT-2-small IOI under zero ablation, largely reproducing Wang et al.'s backup name-mover finding. The record's V3 support from the induction panel is wrong: completion gain measures added damage, not compensation. The V6 evidence is indirect (ranking AUC only).

versions.untested_parts: Layer-level ablation and compensation by later attention layers.
Late-MLP counterbalancing of the maximum-likelihood token, and whether it shrinks when earlier components are ablated. An MLP-group implementation check is mentioned without a reported result.

The study tests head-level recruitment on IOI and held-out repeated-token induction, but not general-text compensation across models using a full-distribution behavioral readout. The cross-model completion measure is induction log-probability.
The study reports partial behavioral preservation and variation across prompt seeds and conditions, but does not report overcorrection beyond the original effect.
Backup name-mover heads are tested. Copy-suppression heads, anti-erasure neurons, and final LayerNorm rescaling as a distinct self-repair mechanism are not established here.
Mean, resample, and Gaussian replacement are tested on GPT-2-small IOI; the alternative operators are not tested across the full model panel.
Tests whether intact-state scores miss backup roles in the studied circuits; it does not measure the direction or size of attribution error for all components or behaviors.
